The bug is in `xmlParsePubidLiteral`:

```c
buf = xmlMalloc(size);  // size = XML_PARSER_BUFFER_SIZE = 100
...
while ((IS_PUBIDCHAR_CH(cur)) && (cur != stop) && (PARSER_STOPPED(ctxt) == 0)) {
    if (len + 1 >= size) {  // when len+1 >= 100, i.e. len >= 99
        xmlChar *tmp;
        int newSize;

        newSize = xmlGrowCapacity(size, 1, 1, maxLength);  // newSize = 150 (grow by 50%)
        if (newSize < 0) {
            ...
        }
        tmp = xmlRealloc(buf, size);  // BUG: uses old `size` (100), not `newSize` (150)
        if (tmp == NULL) {
            ...
        }
        buf = tmp;
        size = newSize;  // size is now 150, but buf is still 100 bytes!
    }
    buf[len++] = cur;  // when len = 99, writes buf[99] (still within 100-byte buffer)
    NEXT;
    cur = CUR;
}
buf[len] = 0;  // when len = 100, writes buf[100] which is OUT OF BOUNDS (buffer is 100 bytes, indices 0-99)
```

But the grow branch uses `xmlRealloc(buf, size)` with the OLD size (100), so the buffer stays at 100 bytes. Then `size = newSize` (150). size_t xmlFuzzReadInt(int size) {
```c
    size_t ret = 0;
    while ((size > 0) && (fuzzData.remaining > 0)) {
        unsigned char c = (unsigned char) *fuzzData.ptr++;
        fuzzData.remaining--;
        ret = (ret << 8) | c;
        size--;
    }
    return ret;
}
```
